thread:
maria: heads-up — we need a quick design for per-API-key burst windows for internal scheduler/batch workers. ops team saw a spike last night and the org quota throttled the workers hard. can we carve short bursts for specific keys?
lee: +1. want ability to give internal keys a higher short-term burst without changing org-level steady-state rate.
sam: what's the requirement? how long and how big are bursts?
maria: typical batch run is 30–90s and needs to submit ~3k requests in a minute occasionally. org quota is much lower, so they get throttled and retry storms. we want per-key burst window like 60s with a configurable token budget.
jordan: sounds like token-bucket per-key on top of org-level enforcement. token-bucket params: capacity and refill_rate. enforce both layers: global org token-bucket + per-key burst allowance that draws from a reserved pool.
alex: question: where to implement? edge gateway or backend service? edge is ideal for early rejections and consistent metrics. but we need config sync across regions.
priya: add to console: UI to set "burst_window_seconds" and "burst_capacity" per key (editable only for internal/partner keys). show recent burst consumption graphs. also audit log entry whenever override used.
ops-bot: incident:scheduler-22 created — last-night batch run hit org rate limit 3x, autoscaler triggered retries. link: https://rwd/incident/22
lee: implementation sketch: gateway maintains per-key bucket with two counters: "steady_bucket" (shared across org) and "burst_bucket" (per-key, resets with sliding window). authentication middleware reads key metadata (flags: internal=true, burst_capacity=3000, burst_window=60). if burst_bucket.tokens>0 allow; else consult steady_bucket.
maria: config example we discussed:
```json
{"api_key_id":"key_abc123","internal":true,"burst_capacity":3000,"burst_window_seconds":60,"steady_qps":10}
```
sam: we'll need metrics: prometheus metrics per key are heavy. suggest emitting labeled metrics for keys tagged as "internal" only and aggregated by team. metric names: `rwd_rate_allow{key_type="internal"}` and `rwd_rate_deny{reason="burst_exhausted"}`. also expose a per-key TTLed ledger for debugging.
jordan: security concern: partner keys could be abused if granted big bursts. require an approvals flow and an expiration timestamp on overrides. also enforce per-org maximum burst footprint so many keys can't blow past capacity.
alex: test plan: unit tests for token-bucket transitions, integration test with gateway + config-store sync, chaos test with simultaneous 10 keys hitting bursts. add e2e in staging where we simulate batch job.
priya: console wire note: show a small popup when applying override: "This override grants temporary extra capacity for X seconds. Requires approval from Platform Eng."
maria: rollout: feature-flag the gateway behavior (off by default). onboard 1 internal team, monitor deny rates, latency, and cost. can we also add automatic fallback to cheaper model variant when throttled?
sam: fallback is separate but useful. gateway can return a header `x-rwd-burst-used: true` so clients can switch to lower-cost path.
lee: ops concerns: billing and attribution — need to ensure per-token accounting for these bursts and tag usage so finance can reconcile.
priya: UX: add filter in key list for "has override" and history tab for each key that lists override events with approver and expiry.
maria: action items: 1) sam & lee: prototype token-bucket in gateway and config schema. 2) priya: mockup console flow and approval modal. 3) jordan: draft security policy for partner overrides. 4) alex: write tests + rollout plan. I'll track in RFC-127.
jordan: small nit — use sliding-window leaky-bucket semantics for burst_bucket to avoid synchronized refill spikes.
lee: ack. will prototype as leaky bucket with per-second drain.
maria: thanks. if nobody objects I'll open the PR tomorrow and feature-flag it behind `per_key_burst_override`. :thumbsup:
